text:
michelle: Heads-up — ran the nightly microbatch sweep after the scheduler change in PR 9402 and I'm seeing a ~12% memory uplift on 2k token longseqs when batch_size <= 8. attaching bench artifacts: http://artifacts.redwood.com/bench/1767771234 :eyes:

omar: ack. can you paste the exact command you used?

michelle: sure —
```
./scripts/run_microbench.sh --model redwood/llama-2-13b --seq 2048 --batch 8 --runs 50 --profile mem,latency 
```
results are in the link above and there's an html diff at artifacts/summary.html

luca: quick question — is this the scheduler patch that switched to the latency-first heuristics (the one that prefers smaller batches on hot shards)?

michelle: yes — that's the one (PR 9402). Timing looks like: after the switch we have more small-batch placements which lowers avg latency but seems to increase per-host resident set for these longseqs.

jay: interesting. do we have a heap/profile flame for the increased RSS? might be memory fragmentation or more kv-shard copies.

michelle: bench-bot attached a psuedo-profile snapshot to the artifact (bench-bot:upload). main diff points to more active arena allocations in runtime allocator and slightly heavier kv-cache header counts.

bench-bot: uploaded mem-profiles/1767771234/ (gz) and a perf map. link: http://artifacts.redwood.com/bench/1767771234/mem-profiles.tgz :white_check_mark:

omar: can we reproduce with a single-host isolated run? if it's shard-placement related it should disappear when forcing single placement.

michelle: good idea. running single-host now, will post results shortly.

sre-oncall: FYI if this reg makes dedicated nodes hit oom margins we should hold auto-rollouts for next cadence. tagging infra to watch. :warning:

luca: while michelle repros, can someone eyeball whether the scheduler's placement added a small-copy path for kv metadata? that's a cheap change to revert if needed.

jay: i'll glance; if it's just extra copy-on-write header we can short-circuit it.

michelle: single-host run: batch 8 -> memory uplift drops to ~2% (within noise). so this is indeed placement/sharding dependent. artifacts updated.

omar: confirms placement. so options: revert scheduler change, tweak shard packing rules, or reduce small-batch bias threshold.

luca: my preference is to tweak the bias threshold and add a guarded canary flag. less risky than revert. also need a post-merge smoke that runs the longseq mem bench.

michelle: agree. i've left a comment on PR 9402 with the canary flag suggestion and attached the bench links. asking for 2nd +1s to unblock a quick follow-up PR that tweaks threshold.

jay: +1 to the guarded flag approach. can we get an approval from runtime leads? @omar @luca please? :thumbsup:

omar: +1, but please include the single-host smoke in CI and make the flag default-off with opt-in in prod for the rollout.

luca: +1. also add an alert that triggers if p95 mem increases > 8% for a week after rollout.

michelle: thanks everyone. i'll push the follow-up PR today (will ping in this thread). if anyone wants to review the canary config early DM me and i'll share the diff. :rocket:

bench-bot: note: nightly microbatch sweep scheduled 02:00 UTC — will re-run after follow-up PR merges.

sre-oncall: noted. monitoring hooks at infra are on standby.

michelle: follow-up PR link (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9461 — requesting 2nd approvals and a short CI run (mem smoke + single-host longseq).
